{{Quote|I don't need to remind you that a crimson blade doesn't guarantee that the wielder is a Sith, any more than every person strong in the Force is a Jedi. Asajj Ventress was a mere apprentice to Dooku, not a true Sith. A crimson blade can owe to nothing more than a synthetic power crystal. Then crimson is simply a color, like Master Windu's amethyst blade.|[[Roan Shryne]]|<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>}}
A '''Synthetic lightsaber crystal''', commonly referred to as a '''Synth-crystal''', was a type of [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|lightsaber crystal]] that was artificially created, rather than naturally formed by geological processes. Due to the methods used in their creation, they were often formed with a red coloration, though they could be made with any color through special manipulations of either the creation process or the crystal itself, often through the Force, such as the [[Color/Legends|green]] synth-crystal that powered [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] [[Luke Skywalker's green lightsaber/Legends|second lightsaber]].<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref>

==Specifications==
===Description===
[[File:VaderSynthCrystal.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The red-hued synth-crystal powering [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] lightsaber.]]
Though synthetic crystals were ordinarily unsuitable for use in [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] discovered that they could create synth-crystals that were energized, magnetized, and modified with the power of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] in special furnaces, causing the crystal to glow in harmonic vibration. As a result of their artificial origins, synthetic crystals created more powerful lightsaber blades and could be more easily augmented. Also, their common usage by Sith and other Darksiders after this discovery caused synthetic crystals to become something of a staple among such groups, and their use among Jedi was strongly discouraged.<ref name="JATM" />

Most synthetic crystals were red, a result of the forging process, and often times the initiate's intentional manipulations, as most individuals who utilized synthetic crystals were Darksiders. The red-hued lightsaber blades generated by such crystals were often nicknamed "bloodshine blades". The crystal's ability to change to reflect the intentions of the creator could be said to foster a stronger bond between the resulting lightsaber and the wielder. However, synth-crystals could be made in any color, requiring only slight adjustments of the creation process and special manipulations through the Force during the forging.

===Creation===
[[File:SithCrystals-FF119.png|thumb|left|150px|A batch of synthetic crystals]]

Synthetic lightsaber crystals were manufactured within a machine known as a geological compressor. The original purpose of the compressor was to replicate geological conditions on distant worlds in a laboratory setting, and it was easily adapted for creating synth-crystals; simply replicating the geological processes that create crystals. The raw materials that the crystal was fashioned from were easily accessible, simply being minerals with a high carbon concentration. The raw minerals would be placed within the machine and essentially left to bake for a period ranging from twenty-four hours to four days, during which time, the initiate creating the crystal would meditate on it with the Force, guiding the formation and increasing the potency. This level of control over the formation process allowed initiates to create crystals that best suited their needs.<ref name="JATM" /><ref name="DMSH">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref>

====Variants====
{{Quote|This synthetic crystal is stronger than the one powering your lightsaber now, and it is much, much stronger than the natural crystals the Jedi use in their own weapons.|[[Qordis]]|<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Uncompressed_Red_Lightsaber_Starkiller_Ultra-Cybog.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Sith lightsaber with a blade generated by an unstable synth-crystal.]]
In addition to the numerous colors synthetic crystals could be fabricated in, there were also variations in the crystals themselves that affected how they focused lightsabers blades.<ref name="JATM" />

'''Standard'''

A standard synthetic crystal was created through the successful replication of the geological structure of natural crystals. Standard crystals set the baseline for synthetic crystals in general; they generated a more powerful lightsaber blade than natural crystals, and often demonstrated a red coloration, though that was easily controlled.<ref name="JATM" /> In fact, synth-crystal blades were so powerful that they had the rare potential to "break the blade" of a standard lightsaber by overloading the energy matrix and instantly burning out the other lightsaber. Though this happened extremely rarely, it was a known and frightening possibility in combat.<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

However, synth-crystal-generated lightsaber blades were generally less manoeuvrable than the blades generated by natural crystals, and were generally more unstable.<ref name="JvS" />

'''Compressed'''

Compressed synth-crystals were a result of a failure to accurately replicate the natural geological process that formed crystals. The result was a crystal that was far more compressed than natural crystals, causing the blade generated to be considerably thinner than standard blades. However, a byproduct of this thinner blade was that it allowed for greater precision and control.<ref name="JATM" /> In addition to a thinner blade, the other visual indicators for a blade generated by a compressed synth-crystal were oscillations of energy that rapidly ran along the length of the blade at regular intervals.<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref>

'''Unstable'''

Like compressed crystals, unstable crystals were the result of the initiate failing to accurately replicate the natural formation processes of crystals. The blades generated by unstable crystals were obviously more unstable than the norm, causing the blades generated to crackle with energy at erratic intervals, sometimes causing sparks to fly or streaks of electrical energy to run along the length. Due to the energy sparking from the blade, unstable synth-crystals caused more damage than normal when they hit enemies. However, they were much more prone to shorting out, causing the lightsaber to deactivate for a time.<ref name="JATM" />

==History==
{{Quote|At my request, the armorer analyzed the Sith lightsaber that I'd recovered from Wud Mortall. She confirmed that his lightsaber contained synthetic crystals, as did every other Sith lightsaber she ever examined.|[[Pernicar]]|<ref name="JvS" />}}
[[File:Red_Color_Crystal.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A synthetic crystal]]
It is unknown when the Sith and other Dark side groups began using synthetic crystals, though red crystals have been in use since the days of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Old Sith Empire]], with notables such as [[Karness Muur]] and his followers wielding such weapons.<ref name="kotor25" /> However, by [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], most Sith wielded [[Sith sword]]s rather than lightsabers,<ref name="golden2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Golden Age of the Sith'' 2]]</ref> though red lightsabers would become the standard weapon after the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reformation of the Empire]].<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

The first Sith-follower to take up a red-bladed weapon before the resurgence of the old Empire was the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Haazen]],<ref name="KotOR 32">[[Knights of the Old Republic 32|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 32]]</ref> as the previous [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] in power; [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]]; and his [[Brotherhood of the Sith|followers]] simply continued using their Jedi lightsabers in combat.<ref name="darklords">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith]]''</ref><ref name="sithwar">''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War]]''</ref> Darths [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak|Malak]] followed suit when they rose to power, making the usage of red-crystals widespread among their Sith followers. Due to their common use within Revan's Sith Empire, red-hued crystals were marked as the staple of Darksiders.<ref name="KOTOR1" />

The primary reason for the usage of synthetic crystals among Sith and other Darksiders was the need to stay hidden, as most of the sites where natural crystals suitable for lightsabers could be gathered were frequented by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Eventually, synth-crystal usage among such groups became a tradition, with most members considering the creation of a synthetic crystal superior to the more passive Jedi method of gathering of natural formations, which was looked on as relying on the "untamed wilds of space" to provide. In fact, synthetic crystal creation was viewed by Darksiders to be a sign of greater mastery over the Force.<ref name="JATM" />

[[File:LukeLightsaberConstruction.png|thumb|right|200px|Luke Skywalker's green synthetic crystal.]]

Conversely, the Jedi frowned on the creation and use of synth-crystals among their initiates, associating this with taking the quick and easy path, as they believed they should rely on crystals found naturally.<ref name="JATM" /> However, sometimes Jedi were forced to create synth-crystals when a weapon was needed and no naturally occurring crystals were accessible. Notable examples include [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], who used a synth-crystal for his [[Luke Skywalker's green lightsaber/Legends|second lightsaber]], because he had no knowledge of the natural crystals at that point, and his niece [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]]. Synth-crystals made by the Jedi usually had colors other than red, to avoid similarities with the Sith. Skywalker created a green crystal, while Solo produced a violet one.<ref name="JvS" />

In fact, because [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] had most of the sites where crystals occurred naturally looted or destroyed during the reign of the Galactic Empire, the [[New Jedi Order]] had to rely on synth-crystals almost exclusively.<ref name="JvS" />

The [[Imperial Knight]]s crafted their [[Imperial Knight lightsaber|lightsabers]] that featured synthetic crystals, using knowledge from Sidious' [[The Book of Anger|Book of Anger]], in a process bereft of ceremony or significance. To an Imperial Knight, a lightsaber was merely a tool, and their training devoted as much attention to fighting in vehicles, bare-handed, and with the Force. The blades of these lightsabers were uniformly a silver-white color.<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

Not all red lightsaber crystals were synthetic. [[Adegan crystal/Legends|Adegan crystals]] featuring a red coloration were not unheard of, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] utilizing such a crystal in one of his lightsabers,<ref name="2013FF1">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File Part 1 (2013)|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' Part 1 <small>(2013)</small>]] {{c|LIG 9-12: Darth Vader's Lightsaber}}</ref> and red-hued crystals were known to form naturally in the [[Crystal Cave (Dantooine)|Crystal Cave]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], along with blue, green, yellow and violet crystals. However, unlike the other crystals, the red crystals from Dantooine were typically found in unhatched [[Kinrath/Legends|kinrath]] eggs.<ref name="KOTOR1" />

==Behind the scenes==
The concept of synthetic lightsaber crystals originated in ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'', the first ever [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying-game]] sourcebook, written by [[Bill Slavicsek]] and [[Curtis Smith]], and published in [[October]] [[1987]] by [[West End Games]].<ref name="sourcebook">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> 

Synthetic crystals subsequently appeared in several stories in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], including the [[Return of the Jedi (radio)|''Return of the Jedi'' radio drama]] and the [[Star Wars: Young Jedi Knights|''Young Jedi Knights'' novels]]. Despite this, ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'' initially claimed that lightsaber crystals could not be synthesized,<ref>''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> a statement that was reiterated in ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'',<ref name="FF53">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 53|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 53]] {{c|LIG 9-12: Darth Vader's Lightsabre [sic]}}</ref> although this was corrected in later editions of those publications.<ref name="2013FF1" /><ref>''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]'' established that the [[Order of the Sith Lords]] preferred synthetic lightsaber crystals<ref name="DMSH" /> and ''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]'' established that to be why Sith lightsabers are red.<ref name="visual">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>
